0.title: Meeting to inform December Market Square report
0.text: A meeting is scheduled this week under item 4 of the resolution. It will inform the report to the December Council meeting.

2.title: Update referred to December resolution
2.text: Council refers readers to resolution 290 from the December meeting for the Market Square update.

4.title: Amenities upgrade complete; March motion scheduled
4.text: The amenities upgrade finished in February. A further Market Square motion is due at the March Council meeting, and weekly reports to councillors continue.

6.title: Meeting with Region Group scheduled
6.text: General Manager and Council staff have scheduled a meeting with Region Group on 21 May 2026.

8.title: Building management scope being discussed
8.text: Region, Council and Strata Choice have begun defining the building and centre management work required. Knight Frank will remain in place during procurement, but will not be invited to tender for the replacement service.

10.title: Lift and escalator tender precedes management tender
10.text: Knight Frank is preparing the lift and escalator maintenance tender for the Building Management Committee. On 11 September, the committee decided to tender for building and centre management only after the maintenance tender is complete and a contractor appointed.

12.title: Crossing lighting design underway
12.text: Lighting design is underway for the raised crossing at Karilla Avenue and Centennial Avenue. The next steps depend on Ausgrid and Transport for NSW approval.

14.text: The lighting design must be finalised before Ausgrid can estimate the installation timing.

16.title: Karilla line markings added to works program
16.text: The Karilla Avenue line markings required by Transport for NSW have been added to Council’s works program.

18.title: Karilla raised crossing construction starts
18.text: Construction has started on the raised crossing at Karilla Avenue and Centennial Avenue. The additional Karilla Avenue line markings are included in the project.

20.title: Line marking installation expected shortly
20.text: Line marking installation is expected shortly.

22.title: Works complete; 40 km/h approval awaited
22.text: Civil works and line marking are complete. Signs are installed but covered while Council waits for Transport for NSW to inspect the area and approve the 40 km/h limit.

24.text: Transport for NSW has inspected the works and requested minor changes. The Mindarie Street and Kullah Parade lighting must be operational before the 40 km/h zone can be approved.

26.text: A lighting contractor has been engaged and is ordering supplies. Supply availability will determine the installation timing.

28.text: The Lane Cove North 40 km/h speed limit is now in force. Staff will carry out the review required by item 8.

30.text: Negotiations with URM continue, and Council has applied to the Environment Protection Authority for a food scraps rollout grant.

32.title: Contractor negotiations continue
32.text: Negotiations with the collection contractor and disposal provider continue. Councillors are to receive an update at the July workshop.

36.title: Food scraps rollout and public information begin
36.text: The rollout began on 1 November 2025. Public information activities start at Lane Cove Plaza on 7 November.

38.title: Rollout update referred to another resolution
38.text: Council refers readers to resolution 180 for the ongoing rollout.

228.text: Council has advised the new owner that developer contributions and a planning agreement are required before a construction certificate. The existing agreement must either be transferred to the new party or replaced; either approach may require 28 days of public exhibition.

234.text: The legal case and banner design are both in progress.

236.text: Council welcomed proposed NSW laws in April 2025 to increase tree vandalism penalties and protect tree canopy. It is contributing to the proposed changes and will publish its input online.

238.text: The legal matter is continuing. Council expects it to be finalised shortly.

448.text: The 22 May councillor bulletin included tenant concerns, the maintenance and improvement plan, and proposed timing.

452.text: The draft Bike Plan is due at the August Council meeting. Its delivery will depend on priorities in Council’s strategic and operational plans and on available budgets and grants.

456.text: A purchase order has been raised, the invoice received and payment authorised. The gallery director has signed and returned the agreement, with thanks from the board.

458.text: Seven councillors have expressed interest in the national local government assembly. Five have confirmed arrangements.

460.text: Staff have obtained training prices and are discussing participation options with the People and Culture team.

464.text: The letters required by items 2 and 3 have been drafted and are due to be sent shortly.

468.title: Lane Cove North shops report due before year end
468.text: The final report is due to Council before the end of the year.

470.text: Letters have been sent to finalise the outgoing and incoming independent expert members of the Local Planning Panel.

472.title: Planning participation letters sent
472.text: Letters were sent to the Planning Minister, Lane Cove MP and Bennelong MP on 1 May. Councillors will be updated on responses. A future Council report will cover the NSW Government’s Statewide Community Participation Plan.

474.text: Staff will provide advice in the councillor bulletin before 30 June on the volunteer CPR trainer pathway requested in item 4.

478.text: Council adopted the 2026/27 budget in June. Letters reflecting the grant decisions have been sent, and the grants ceremony is scheduled for 5 August 2026.

480.text: Council notes the May meeting decision and associated resolution.

484.text: The Sustainability Team has told the Organic Buyer Group that Council supports the program. The group is coordinating venue bookings and promotion with Council teams.

486.text: The National Cultural Policy submission has been lodged. Council’s record reference is 40228/2026.

488.text: Council has written to thank Jacky Barker for providing a platform for resident views and promoting local businesses, events and volunteering.

490.title: No further progress on sports field allocation report

492.text: The sports allocation matters will be considered in the management directive review under resolution 284/2025.

502.text: Letters were sent to the NSW Roads, Transport and Youth ministers on 15 July. Council’s road safety officers are developing an e-bike education campaign.

504.text: The Road Safety Team attended a Lime Bike event at the Plaza, and the Youth Team ran a workshop with NSW Police. Staff have formed an internal group to develop further safety activities and grant options.

506.text: The required correspondence has been sent and the action plan provided to the NSW Ombudsman. A further Council report will follow once the plan is completed to the Ombudsman’s satisfaction.

508.title: Youth policy submission lodged before deadline
508.text: The submission was sent to the NSW Office for Youth before the 30 June deadline.

510.title: Federal inquiry submission published
510.text: The submission was sent to the federal inquiry and published on Council’s website.

512.text: Council has sent the letter requested by item 2 to North Shore Police Area Command.

514.text: Letters have been sent to the NSW Education and Early Learning Minister and Deputy Premier.

516.text: The letters required by items 2, 3 and 4 have been sent.

520.text: Council has lodged an expression of interest in the Global Urban Data Centres Pact, following action on items 2 and 3. The Mayor, Deputy Mayor and General Manager met the program team on 1 October. Staff are preparing a report on possible formal endorsement.

522.title: Letters sent; public guidance update to follow
522.text: Letters have been sent to the NSW Fair Trading Minister and the relevant federal ministers about an import ban. Updates to guidelines and public information are still to follow.

524.text: Staff are reviewing the website information required by item 5.

526.text: Staff are carrying out the actions in item 3 to prepare the October Council report.

530.text: The submission was sent to the Office of Local Government on 3 August. Councillors received a copy in the 7 August bulletin.

532.text: The conference motion will be submitted after the September Council report finalises the additional proposed motions.

534.text: Letters were sent to the principals of Lane Cove Public, Greenwich Public and Lane Cove West Public schools on 24 August 2026.

536.text: Letters were sent to state ministers on 7 September about waste planning. Council highlighted its Resilient Sydney membership and the General Manager’s waste leadership role. It supports coordinated advocacy through Resilient Sydney and regional council organisations, and asks the NSW Government to work with them on long-term solutions.

538.title: Space-use research and report preparation begin
538.text: Research into use of the space has begun, along with drafting the report.

540.text: The draft financial statements for the year ending 30 June 2026 have been sent to the NSW Audit Office for audit.

542.title: Asylum seeker taskforce membership remains active
542.text: Council’s membership remains active, continuing its participation in the Mayoral Taskforce Supporting People Seeking Asylum.

544.text: The draft plan is on public exhibition.

548.text: Council has sent the letters to Cameraygal Wind Symphony required by items 2 and 3.

552.text: Council has lodged its response to the Local Government Performance Ratios Discussion Paper with the Office of Local Government.

554.text: Council has sent the submission to the Grants Commission required by item 1.
